title: Give decisions log an explicit --feature so Discovery can attribute its own work
action: Add --feature <slug> to bee decisions log (decision-attribution D2). An explicit value ALWAYS wins over the calling session's bound lane; with neither, the event carries no feature key (D1, already landed in da-1). Steps: (1) add `feature: Option<String>` to LogParams in verbs/decisions/verbs_read.rs and update every constructor - 33 in decisions/tests.rs, plus verbs_read.rs:238 and three in state_group/set_gate.rs - passing None where the caller has no opinion. (2) parse the flag in run_log and pass it through. (3) in do_log, prefer the explicit value over feature_for_stamp(&target). (4) validate the slug: reject empty or whitespace-only with a typed FIX line naming the flag - never silently ignore it. (5) DECLARE the flag in generated/registry_payload.json - a flag served but not declared gives the CLI-shape guard no schema, and tests/registry_dispatch.rs enforces both directions. Edit that file as DATA, never as text: it is one line of JSON.

truths: An explicit --feature stamps that value even when the session is bound to a different lane
An explicit --feature stamps that value when no lane is bound at all - the Discovery case D2 exists for
With no --feature and a bound lane, the lane still wins (da-1 behaviour unchanged)
With no --feature and no bound lane, the event still carries no feature key
An empty or whitespace-only --feature refuses with a typed FIX line naming the flag, and writes nothing
bee --help shows the flag, and tests/registry_dispatch.rs stays green in both directions
